source.title: Self-Destructive Language Model
source.authors: Yu-Hui Wang; Rong-Yi Zhu; Ting Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning and benign fine-tuning effects on harmful-response measures using different models, settings, and measures. It also tests whether adding diverse refusal responses improves resistance to an orthogonalization attack.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own harmful fine-tuning and benign fine-tuning evaluations, plus an orthogonalization-attack result after adding diverse refusals. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-token prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, or localization of safety to a small set of parameters. Cited claims about prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study's undefended baselines bear on V1. Five safety-tuned chat models (Llama2-7b-chat, Qwen2.5-3b/7b, Llama3.2-3b, Llama3.1-8b) were fine-tuned on 1K BeaverTails harmful pairs. Harmfulness, scored by a classifier and checked with GPT-4o, rises sharply. The baselines also bear on V2: an Alpaca-only fine-tune (p=0.0) and a sensitive-but-benign OR-Bench fine-tune. A 500-example extended-refusal fine-tune, described as spreading refusal across token positions, was tested against orthogonalization, which bears on V7. Results on SEAM-defended models are the study's own method and do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SEAM keeps benign utility and fine-tunability while making harmful fine-tuning self-defeating: weak attacks leave harmfulness low, and strong attacks collapse the model's capabilities. They also note that undefended aligned models are easily compromised by harmful fine-tuning. Adding extended-refusal examples reduces, but does not remove, vulnerability to orthogonalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a new alignment-stage defense, S EAM, using BeaverTails harmful fine-tuning attacks and harmfulness/zero-shot measures; it does not reproduce the original studies' measurements of token-position KL or compliant-opening effects.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with attack learning rate and model. The paper also varies harmful sample count, fine-tuning method, optimizer, mixed-data contamination, and other attack settings; the alternative-model results include exceptions where S EAM HS rises.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight orthogonalization (refusal-direction ablation) jailbreaks undefended Llama-2-7B-chat with ASR 0.99 and the SEAM model with ASR 0.98 (Table 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating a single refusal direction in the weights removes refusal in safety-tuned chat models.

fits_no_version.finding: In PCA, gradients on harmful and benign batches are inseparable in the undefended model (Figure 6). The authors offer this as a partial explanation of why benign fine-tuning erodes safety.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign and harmful fine-tuning gradients point in similar directions in aligned models.

fits_no_version.finding: SEAM-defended models keep HS low under harmful fine-tuning, but at high learning rates their utility collapses (ZS about 25%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-coupling defenses trade harmful trainability for model collapse.

record.problems: The main reported harmful fine-tuning sample sizes are 1K and 10K, outside the claim's few-to-few-hundred range. The study uses a classifier-based harmfulness score for its main measure, with GPT-4o assessment reported as an additional check. Some additional attack results are presented only in figures or appendices.
record.rows_left_out: Not all additional attack conditions were extracted: Figure 3 reports multiple 10K-sample, LoRA, and SGD attack settings, and Tables 9-13 and 15-20 report further adaptive attacks, ablations, and capability measures. These were omitted to prioritize the 1K harmful fine-tuning sweeps across models, benign fine-tuning outcomes, and the extended-refusal result; none directly tests token-position KL or compliant-opening bypass.

untested.parts: Pure harmful fine-tunes below 1K examples; the few-example range appears only inside the mixed-data setup (Table 2), which no row records. Refusal-rate measures were not used.
Benign datasets beyond Alpaca (one setting) and OR-Bench; few-shot benign fine-tuning; benign data chosen to break safety.
Not tested: no per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Not tested: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Not tested: no localization of safety to a small set of weights or ranks. The orthogonalization attack is a direction ablation, not a parameter-localization test.
No token-position measure of whether the extended-refusal fine-tune deepens safety. Not tested against harmful fine-tuning or prefilling. Not tested without SEAM.

missing.what: Undefended Llama2-7b-chat under mixed harmful/Alpaca data. HS rises from 5.0 to 12.6 at p=0.01 (about 10 harmful of 1K), 27.5 at p=0.05, 50.9 at p=0.10 and 76.6 at p=0.20. This covers the few-to-few-hundred range V1 names.
GPT-4o HS-G for undefended Llama2-7b-chat after harmful fine-tuning: 1.0 pre-attack, then 44.7, 71.0, 77.0, 74.0 and 76.0 across learning rates. This is an alternative judge for V1.
Undefended model under further harmful-attack variants. With a benign-task regularizer, HS is 77.5 down to 65.7 as lambda rises. On unseen-domain harmful data, HS is 27.1-79.6.

record.verdict_notes: Harmful fine-tuning uses 1K samples, more than the 'few hundred' in V1. The few-example evidence exists only in the mixed-data Table 2, which no row records. The main harmfulness measure is a BeaverTails classifier logit score, which may react to affirmative keywords; GPT-4o HS-G broadly agrees. The reader's V1 limits_scope label rested on SEAM rows and is dropped, because those rows evaluate the authors' own defense. High HS in SEAM rows (e.g. R18) coincides with incoherent output. Table 12's undefended numbers are identical to Table 6's, so they may have been reused.

versions.untested_parts: Tests attacks with 1K and 10K harmful samples, not the claimed few-to-few-hundred range. It does not directly report refusal rates for all fine-tuning conditions.

Tests Alpaca-only fine-tuning in a mixed-data attack setup and a 2,000-prompt sensitive-but-benign OR-Bench fine-tune; it does not test a broad range of ordinary benign instruction datasets or few-example benign fine-tuning.
Tests an added refusal-response dataset against orthogonalization, but not training explicitly to spread safety across response positions or its robustness to other attacks.
